screening.reason: Inclusion 2/3: analyses ABIDE resting-state fMRI (single-volume brain images derived from rs-fMRI) explicitly and reports an ASD-vs-control diagnostic classification analysis.

evidence_spans.text: We incorporated data from 529 ASD individuals and 573 typical controls (TC) for each pipeline, which is comprised of 17 different imaging sites.
evidence_spans.claim: Cohort: 529 ASD and 573 typical control individuals from 17 ABIDE sites, processed with each of four pipelines.

evidence_spans.text: Selected strategies are Connectome Computation System (CCS), Conﬁgurable Pipeline for the Analysis of Con- nectomes (CPAC), Data Processing Assistant for Resting-State fMRI (DPARSF) and Neuroimaging Analysis Kit (NIAK).
evidence_spans.claim: Four Preprocessed Connectomes Project pipelines (CCS, C-PAC, DPARSF, NIAK) were used in parallel.

evidence_spans.text: in this work, ﬁrstly, we design an image genera- tor to generate single volume brain images from the whole-brain image of each subject.
evidence_spans.claim: Features are single-volume whole-brain images generated per subject, rather than ROI-based connectivity matrices.

evidence_spans.text: we ﬁrst divided the whole dataset into two parts: training (85%), and testing (15%). From the generated training images, approximately 85% of the whole images were considered as the training set, and 15% as the validation set.
evidence_spans.claim: Evaluation used a single random 85/15 train/test split rather than cross-validation.

evidence_spans.text: Table V represents the classiﬁcation performance for ensemble learning showing that the third ensemble classiﬁer performs better than other ensembles.
evidence_spans.claim: A deep ensemble classifier (VGG16 feature extractor) was the best-performing of four ensemble configurations tested.

evidence_spans.text: In our experiments, the highest accuracy for glass brain images is up to 85% belongs to several data sites and for stat map images the accuracy is up to 84% for several data sites as shown in the table.
evidence_spans.claim: Unit-site classification reached up to 85% accuracy (glass-brain images) and 84% (stat-map images) for some individual sites.

evidence_spans.text: therefore we performed unit-site classiﬁcation to pattern out
evidence_spans.claim: Per-site (unit-site) classification was performed to characterise inter-site variability.

assessments.support: 529 ASD and 573 TC from 17 ABIDE sites, processed identically across four pipelines; phenotypic table (sex, age, ADOS) reported.
Four named preprocessing pipelines (CCS, C-PAC, DPARSF, NIAK) explicitly compared with a table of per-pipeline processing steps; single-volume image generator method described in detail.
ASD/TC label drawn from ABIDE phenotypic data; ADOS reported for subgroup but the specific diagnostic criteria used to assign ASD/TC are not restated.

Primary evaluation is a single random 85%/15% train/test split (no cross-validation, no uncertainty estimate across repeated splits) despite pooling data across 17 sites without leave-site-out evaluation for the main classifier.

risk_of_bias.summary: Well-documented multi-pipeline ABIDE cohort and preprocessing comparison, but the primary classification evaluation relies on a single random train/test split without cross-validation or site-held-out testing, limiting confidence in the reported accuracies.

charting.title: Single Volume Image Generator and Deep Learning-Based ASD Classification
charting.authors: Ahmed MR; Zhang Y; Inan OT; Liao H
charting.journal_conference: IEEE Journal of Biomedical and Health Informatics
charting.diagnosis_assessment: ADOS score reported for subset of subjects
charting.feature_types: whole-brain single-volume image (glass-brain and stat-map renderings)
charting.specific_features: Single-volume whole-brain glass-brain and statistical-map images generated per subject from four preprocessing pipelines
charting.feature_extraction_tools: CCS, C-PAC, DPARSF, NIAK (Preprocessed Connectomes Project pipelines)
charting.specific_algorithms: Volume-based CNN; deep ensemble classifier using VGG16 as feature extractor (4 ensemble configurations compared)
charting.validation_methodology: Single random 85%/15% training/testing split; per-site (unit-site) classification also evaluated
charting.key_performance_results: Unit-site classification accuracy up to 85% (glass-brain images) and 84% (stat-map images) for several sites; best ensemble classifier (classifier 3) outperformed other ensemble configurations across all four pipelines
charting.summary_key_findings: A single-volume image generator applied to four ABIDE preprocessing pipelines (CCS, C-PAC, DPARSF, NIAK) combined with CNN and VGG16-based deep ensemble classifiers achieves up to 85% unit-site classification accuracy for ASD vs. typical control, evaluated with a single 85/15 train/test split.

narrative_row.study_design_sample_dataset: Diagnostic prediction; ABIDE I; 529 ASD and 573 typically developing individuals (1102 total) from 17 sites, each processed with four pipelines (CCS, C-PAC, DPARSF, NIAK)
narrative_row.methods: A single-volume image generator converts each subject's whole-brain fMRI volume into glass-brain and stat-map images; CNN and VGG16-based deep ensemble classifiers evaluated with an 85%/15% train/test split, plus per-site (unit-site) classification
narrative_row.outcomes: Unit-site classification accuracy up to 85% (glass-brain) and 84% (stat-map) for several sites; the third deep ensemble classifier configuration performed best across all four pipelines
narrative_row.key_limitations: Single random train/test split with no cross-validation; no leave-site-out evaluation for the pooled multi-site classifier despite known site heterogeneity
narrative_row.relevance_notes: Provides a direct four-pipeline (CCS/C-PAC/DPARSF/NIAK) comparison on the same ABIDE cohort using a non-connectivity (whole-volume image) feature representation
